clue.text: Husband turned up, not very stressed

indicators.note: 'not' asks for removal and 'very' names the letter to go, V being the usual abbreviation for very

parts.note: to turn up is to arrive, so turned up gives arrived

explanation.surface: A husband finally arrives home, claiming he was not especially bothered by anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not very' signals dropping V, the usual abbreviation for very; 'stressed' is the definition, not a hint at emphasis.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone harried has been harassed and worn down by pressure, so is stressed.

clue.text: Central area mostly covered other areas — 11?

parts.note: a hub is a central point of activity

indicators.note: the word for spreading loses its final letter

parts.note: paint or dye that bleeds spreads into neighbouring areas

explanation.surface: A central zone mostly spread into neighbouring ones.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme answers are people with laws named after them: Hubble's law of cosmic expansion.
explanation.definitionFit: Edwin Hubble gave his name to Hubble's law, so he is a lawmaker in the theme's playful sense.

clue.text: Sincere about unpleasant spot being done over in a fresh start

indicators.note: the word for sincere surrounds the other piece

parts.note: real means genuine, sincere

indicators.note: turned over, so the word for the spot is reversed

parts.note: a wen is a cyst or growth on the skin

explanation.surface: An honest blemish gets worked over to make a clean beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being done over' signals the reversal and 'about' the container; a wen is an old word for a skin cyst.
explanation.definitionFit: A renewal is a revival or beginning again, a fresh start.

clue.text: Increasing costs seeing banker finally leaving popular New York building

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: the letter named departs from the building's name

parts.note: the Flatiron Building in Manhattan

indicators.note: the last letter of the word banker

explanation.surface: Rising prices see a banker finally quit a famous Manhattan building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes the R (from 'banker finally') out of FLATIRON.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflation is a general rise in prices across an economy.

clue.text: Unexpectedly nice and kind as … as an author

definitions.note: an adjective meaning like a particular Victorian novelist

indicators.note: something done unexpectedly comes out in a surprising form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is surprisingly nice and as kind as a writer could be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unexpectedly' rearranges NICE, KIND and AS; the ellipsis invites 'as Dickensian as', in the manner of Dickens.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickensian means in the style of Charles Dickens, the Victorian novelist.

clue.text: Senior politician accepting a lot of nonsense by Unionist — it's worthless stuff

indicators.note: PM accepting the other pieces holds them between its two letters

parts.note: PM, the Prime Minister, is the most senior politician

indicators.note: 'a lot of' means most but not all, so the final letter of the word for nonsense is lost

parts.note: bull is slang for nonsense
U is the abbreviation for Unionist in UK politics

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister tolerates a pile of rubbish from a Unionist colleague, dismissed as worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' drops the last letter of the nonsense word, and 'accepting' puts everything inside the senior politician; 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pabulum is bland, insipid intellectual fare, material of little or no value.

clue.text: Make inquiries about a petition

indicators.note: the word for prying goes around the letter

parts.note: to pry is to inquire nosily

explanation.surface: Someone asks questions about a formal petition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A inside PRY.
explanation.definitionFit: To pray is to beg or entreat, which is to petition.

clue.text: The French will support lad, 11?

indicators.note: in a down entry the French word sits below the boy, holding it up

parts.note: a lad is a boy
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: The French will back a young man.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Boyle gave his name to Boyle's law on gas pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Boyle's law, about gas pressure and volume, makes Boyle a lawmaker in the theme's sense.

clue.text: Someone opposed to Prince having a lot of news about Queen

indicators.note: the shortened news goes around the queen's letters
most of the word for news, its last letter dropped

parts.note: the latest is the most recent news
ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: An opponent of royalty has lots of gossip about the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' drops the last letter of the news word; 'about' wraps it round the queen. The Prince is Hamlet.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hamlet, Laertes duels Prince Hamlet, so he is the prince's opponent.

clue.text: 11, perhaps, to be disruptive, interrupting friend

indicators.note: the word for being disruptive breaks into the word for friend

parts.note: a mate is a friend
to riot is to cause public disorder

explanation.surface: A lawmaker makes a scene, cutting in on a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: Edme Mariotte independently found the gas law also called Boyle–Mariotte's law.
explanation.definitionFit: Mariotte's law on gas pressure makes the French physicist a lawmaker in the theme's sense.

clue.text: Recipient of bequest, one tucking into beer, I fancy, getting drunk

indicators.note: the letter for one is put inside the word beer
being drunk leaves things jumbled, so the combined letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone tucks into a beer and decides they fancy getting drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' sets I (one) inside the jumble that 'getting drunk' makes of BEER, I and FANCY; 'one' and 'I' look like the same person, but each gives its own letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A person named in a will who receives property is its beneficiary.

clue.text: Be wary of losing initial attention

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for being wary is dropped

parts.note: to fear something is to be wary of it

explanation.surface: Advice to be careful about losing what was first noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing initial' takes F off FEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone your ear is to listen, so ear here means attention, as in 'lend an ear'.

clue.text: US city to be stirred up about married Republican legislator

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

indicators.note: the word for being roused goes around the letter for married

parts.note: to wake is to be roused or stirred from sleep

explanation.surface: An American city is roused against a married Republican politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be stirred up' looks like an anagram signal, but it is a plain synonym (to wake); 'about' wraps it round the letter for married.
explanation.definitionFit: A legislator is one who makes laws, a member of a law-making body.

clue.text: On the side of number restraining someone drinking again?

indicators.note: the abbreviation for number holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: TT means teetotal, so an ex-TT is a former abstainer back on the drink

explanation.surface: A number keeps back a person who has returned to the bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the cryptic EX-TT, a former teetotaller.
explanation.definitionFit: Beside or alongside something means on its side, adjacent to it.

clue.text: Rubbish about university in province overturning output of 11?

indicators.note: the rubbish piece is put inside the reversed province
in a down entry the name of the province is read upwards

parts.note: Wales is a province, one of the countries of the UK

indicators.note: the word for rubbish surrounds the letter for university

parts.note: tatt, also spelt tat, is cheap rubbish

explanation.surface: Junk around a university is turned upside down by a lawmaker's output.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' and 'in' are both containers; 'overturning' reverses only the province, giving SELAW, which the rubbish piece TATUT enters after its first letter. Wales is called a province here loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: Statute law is legislation passed by a parliament, the product of its legislators.

clue.text: Great care taken about lake in flat land

indicators.note: the word for care is wrapped around the letter for lake

parts.note: to take pains is to take great care

explanation.surface: Great care is taken around a lake set in level country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken about' puts L inside PAINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Plains are wide expanses of level, largely treeless country.

clue.text: Ready to go public? Certainly seizing power during historic offensive

indicators.note: the combined piece sits inside the name of the offensive

parts.note: the Tet Offensive of 1968 in the Vietnam War

indicators.note: the word for certainly takes hold of the letter for power

parts.note: yes is an affirmative, certainly
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A company poised to float, certainly grabbing power amid a famous military attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seizing' and 'during' are nested containers. The Tet Offensive was a 1968 Vietnam War campaign; 'go public' hints at publishing, not a share flotation.
explanation.definitionFit: Text that is typeset has been set in type and is ready for printing and publication.

clue.text: Cleric restricting family 11?

indicators.note: the word for cleric hems in the word for family

parts.note: a parson is a parish priest
kin are family members

explanation.surface: A clergyman keeps his relatives in check.
explanation.walkthrough: C. Northcote Parkinson coined Parkinson's law: work expands to fill the time available.
explanation.definitionFit: Parkinson's law, about work and time, makes its coiner a lawmaker in the theme's sense.

clue.text: Suit trouble after overturning drink

indicators.note: the reversed piece comes after the card suit

parts.note: clubs is one of the four card suits

indicators.note: the word for trouble is read upwards in this down entry

parts.note: ado is fuss, trouble

explanation.surface: A lawsuit brings trouble after a drink is knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' looks legal; it is a suit of cards. 'overturning' turns ADO into ODA.
explanation.definitionFit: Club soda is carbonated water used as a mixer, a drink.

clue.text: Classic mount only somewhat ridable

indicators.note: only part of the word is used, so the letters are taken from within it

explanation.surface: An ancient steed that can only partly be ridden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Classic mount' looks like a horse; it is a mountain of classical myth, Mount Ida.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Ida, in Crete or near Troy, is a mountain famous in Greek mythology.

clue.text: Woman: reduced chance Asian country will deport second one

indicators.note: the word for chance is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: luck is chance

indicators.note: the second of the two letters I (one) in the country is removed

parts.note: India

explanation.surface: A woman's slim chance as an Asian country plans to expel a second person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' trims LUCK to LUC; 'will deport second one' removes the second I from INDIA to leave INDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucinda is a female given name, so it fits a woman.

clue.text: French city supporting church 11?

indicators.note: in a down entry the city sits below the church, holding it up

parts.note: Arles is a city in Provence

explanation.surface: A French city backs its church.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacques Charles gave his name to Charles's law on gas volume and temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles's law, linking gas volume and temperature, makes the physicist a lawmaker in the theme's sense.

clue.text: Impetuous after half of that party

indicators.note: the word for impetuous comes after the half word
only the first two of the four letters of the word that are used

parts.note: rash means impetuous

explanation.surface: Someone acts rashly after half of that party.
explanation.walkthrough: THRASH is British slang for a lively party.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a thrash is a big, lively party or celebration.

clue.text: Dispatched to bring in a Greek character of great wisdom

indicators.note: the word for dispatched takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: sent means dispatched
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone is sent to fetch a very wise Greek figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' looks like a sage; it is a letter, PI.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapient means wise, possessing great wisdom.

clue.text: Academic accommodating key 11?

indicators.note: the word for academic houses the key's letters

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: A lecturer holds the key.
explanation.walkthrough: John Dalton gave his name to Dalton's law of partial pressures.
explanation.definitionFit: Dalton's law, about gas mixtures, makes the chemist a lawmaker in the theme's sense.

clue.text: Monarch put in a lot of money for composer

indicators.note: the monarch's letters go inside the shortened word for money
most of the word for money, its last letter dropped

parts.note: brass is British slang for money
HM stands for His or Her Majesty

explanation.surface: A king invests heavily in a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' drops the last letter of the money word and 'put in' places the monarch inside. Brass is northern English slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Brahms was a German Romantic composer.

clue.text: 11, say, increasingly embracing love

indicators.note: the word for increasingly wraps around the letter

parts.note: more and more, increasingly
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A legislator increasingly embraces love.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon Moore gave his name to Moore's law on the doubling of transistors on chips.
explanation.definitionFit: Moore's law, on computer chip growth, makes Gordon Moore a lawmaker in the theme's sense.

clue.text: A lot of moral work I advanced in African country

indicators.note: most of the word for moral, its last letter dropped

parts.note: an ethic is a moral principle
OP, short for opus, is a work
A stands for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: Much moral work is pushed forward in an African nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' trims ETHIC to ETHI.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethiopia is a nation in the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: Area of land is governed after Democrat steps down

indicators.note: resigns, so the Democrat's letter leaves the word for governed

parts.note: led means governed, directed

explanation.surface: Land is ruled by others after a Democrat resigns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steps down' removes D from LED.
explanation.definitionFit: An isle is an island, a piece of land surrounded by water.

clue.text: Bird not aloft, heading to rear

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for not aloft moves to the back

parts.note: low means not high up

explanation.surface: A bird flies low, heading towards the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading to rear' moves the L of LOW to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An owl is a nocturnal bird of prey.

clue.text: Recalled bad smell, only smell, no longer fresh?

indicators.note: called back, so the letters for bad smell are written in reverse

parts.note: BO is body odour
sole means only
a scent is a smell

explanation.surface: A stink is remembered, just a smell that is past its best.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the stretch: obsolescent things are going out of date, not literally stale.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obsolescent is becoming outdated, losing its newness.

clue.text: Bleak Georgian writer about to put out start of novel

indicators.note: the letter named is expelled and replaced by the word for about

parts.note: Jane Austen wrote in the Georgian era

indicators.note: the first letter of the word novel

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A grim Georgian novelist is about to abandon the opening of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to put out' swaps the N of AUSTEN (from 'start of novel') for RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means severe and plain, bare of comfort, hence bleak.

clue.text: 11, perhaps, secures a great deal

parts.note: to win something is to secure it
tons means a great deal, a ton being a large amount

explanation.surface: Someone clinches a big agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme is laws named after people; Winston Churchill, a parliamentarian, is a lawmaker example.
explanation.definitionFit: Winston Churchill sat in Parliament for decades, making him an example of a legislator.
